items.title: Net-zero pledges remain steady, but top companies show evidence of backtracking
items.summary: The past two years have seen a growing sense that major corporations are watering down their climate commitments, with media reports — including here at Trellis — describing targets being made less ambitious, deadlines delayed and goals silently abandoned.

items.title: What’s at stake for the UK at COP31?
items.summary: With the UK’s clean energy ambitions under the spotlight and its fossil fuel decisions raising awkward questions, COP31 is a chance to show where its climate leadership really stands.

items.title: COP31 Action Tracker: US midterms and Brazil Roadmaps
items.summary: With COP31 in Türkiye starting next week, this regular members-only series from edie provides a temperature check on global climate action, including news from governments and other key organisations ahead of the summit.

items.title: Corporate net-zero targets hold firm while cities lag
items.summary: According to new data, the number of businesses with net-zero targets has remained stable in 2026 despite political headwinds, though gaps across city- and region-specific goals remain.

items.title: Two weeks to register: How to turn climate risk insights into adaptation action
items.summary: This webinar, held in partnership with SmartResilience on 19 November, will explore why and how leading organisations are moving from simply measuring risk to actively adapting in order to protect their operations, assets and supply chains.

items.title: UK to introduce mandatory human rights due diligence law for large businesses
items.summary: The UK Government will introduce mandatory human rights due diligence requirements for large businesses, requiring them to identify, assess and address risks of human rights abuses and labour exploitation in their operations and supply chains.

items.title: Apply now: Entries open for the edie Awards 2027
items.summary: The UK’s largest corporate sustainability awards scheme is celebrating its 20th year with a restructured programme, built around three pillars and new categories including AI, water and adaptation.
